segments.text: How much space does a circle cover? The answer is famous: pi r squared. But why is it true?
Take a circle of radius r, and cut it into equal wedges, like slicing a pizza.
Now unroll it. Lay the wedges side by side, pointing up, then down, then up again.
The pieces interlock into a shape that is almost a parallelogram. Cut more wedges, and the bumpy edges smooth out.
In the limit, it becomes a perfect rectangle. Its height is the radius, r.
Its width is half of the circumference. The whole circumference is two pi r, so half of it is pi r.
Area is width times height. Pi r, times r, gives pi r squared.
And that is why a circle of radius r has area pi r squared.
